clue.text: Frolicking, perhaps Rupert Murdoch once receives fright when naked

indicators.note: receives means the king's title takes another piece inside it

parts.note: Murdoch once controlled Sky, the satellite broadcaster, so he was a Sky king; perhaps marks him as one example

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its outer covering, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: alarm is fright or sudden fear

explanation.surface: A media mogul gets a scare while undressed, and the result is horseplay.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is the British satellite TV company Murdoch's News Corp long controlled. ALARM stripped by 'when naked' leaves LAR, received into SKY KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Skylarking is boisterous playing about, mischievous fun of the kind sailors once got up to in the rigging.

clue.text: Train maybe loses power before opening of Elizabeth Line

parts.note: an engine that dies stops working and loses power

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Elizabeth
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A train on London's new Elizabeth Line suffers a power failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loses power' looks like a deletion of P, but it is simply a synonym for dies, as an engine does.
explanation.definitionFit: A diesel is a locomotive or train driven by a diesel engine, so a train is one possible example.

clue.text: Spies succeeded holding two groups of soldiers roughly

indicators.note: something holding other things has them inside it

parts.note: moles are spies planted inside an organisation
RE (Royal Engineers) and OR (other ranks)
S is the abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: Intelligence agents manage, more or less, to keep hold of some army units.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (Royal Engineers) and OR (other ranks, ordinary soldiers) are standard crossword army units; the S for succeeded goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: 'More or less' is an idiom meaning approximately, which is what roughly means.

clue.text: Excess muscle athlete ultimately shed

indicators.note: something shed has been cast off, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a glute is a buttock muscle

indicators.note: 'ultimately' keeps only the last letter of 'athlete'

parts.note: last letter of athlete

explanation.surface: An athlete finally loses some surplus muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: A glut is an oversupply, a synonym for an excess of something.

clue.text: Cured meat, roast that regularly after time in Rome?

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, to roast
Central European Time is the time zone used in Rome

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, here every other one

parts.note: first and third letters of that

explanation.surface: A query about whether cured ham is roasted in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time in Rome' tempts an Italian word for time, but it means the time zone Italy keeps, Central European Time.
explanation.definitionFit: Pancetta is Italian cured pork belly, a type of cured meat.

clue.text: Avoiding extremes, lives healthily

indicators.note: avoiding extremes means dropping the first and last letters, keeping only the inside

parts.note: dwells means lives, resides

explanation.surface: Moderation in all things is the secret of healthy living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lives' is a verb here, giving DWELLS; 'Avoiding extremes' looks like lifestyle advice but trims it to its interior.
explanation.definitionFit: Well as an adverb means in good health or in a sound manner, as in eating well.

clue.text: Level with Spain in thriller, perhaps

indicators.note: one letter is placed in the other word

parts.note: a thriller is one kind of story
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A thriller set in Spain that keeps things even.
explanation.definitionFit: A storey is one level or floor of a building.

clue.text: Offer finally to travel with Katie, i.e. abroad

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A final offer for Katie to travel overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offer finally' looks like it asks for the last letter of offer, but it is the definition: a final, non-negotiable offer.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Take it or leave it' is said of a final offer that will not be improved by any bargaining.

clue.text: Claiming two hundred exactly initially attended musical work

indicators.note: claiming means taking hold of, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: 'to a T' means exactly
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so CC is two hundred

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the following word

parts.note: first letter of attended

explanation.surface: An audience of exactly two hundred claims to have attended a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a virtuoso keyboard piece, an example of a musical work.

clue.text: Pass handgun over, without its case

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the pistol's name is read backwards
the case is the outer layer, so the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: a Glock is a make of semi-automatic pistol

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to hand over a firearm, leaving its holster behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' looks like a verb telling someone to hand the gun on, but it is a noun. 'without its case' strips GLOCK to LOC, and 'over' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A col is a pass between mountain peaks, the lowest point on a ridge.

clue.text: Show half of viewers abandoned has a copper meeting God!

indicators.note: half of a word means only part of it is kept and the rest discarded

parts.note: spectators are viewers
taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a Lar is a Roman household god

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a show abandoned by half its audience still found a policeman meeting God.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first five of the ten letters of SPECTATORS are kept. Lares were the guardian gods of a Roman household.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacular is a lavish theatrical or television production, a big show.

clue.text: One left to pursue interest in spring time

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow behind, so these pieces are placed after the other one

parts.note: APR is the annual percentage rate of interest
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned to chase a hobby in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To pursue' puts the pair 'One left' after the interest rate.
explanation.definitionFit: April is a month that falls in spring in the northern hemisphere.

clue.text: Quite far behind immediately

parts.note: right means quite or completely, as in 'a right mess'
away means far behind, as in 'away back' or 'way behind'

explanation.surface: A report that someone is trailing well behind straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Right away' is an idiom meaning at once, without delay.

clue.text: Family member imposing on European in foreign resort

parts.note: grand means impressive or imposing

indicators.note: one letter is placed in the word for the resort

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A relative imposing themselves on a European while abroad at a resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand-niece is the granddaughter of one's sibling, a member of the wider family.

clue.text: Winchester chap Keith was my undoing

indicators.note: undoing something takes it apart, so its letters can be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man ruefully admits that Keith from Winchester brought about his downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: Winchester College is a famous English public (private boarding) school founded by William of Wykeham.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wykehamist is a past or present pupil of Winchester College, named after its founder.

clue.text: Artist blowing top about Universal in dispute

indicators.note: about means around, so the word wraps round a letter
to blow one's top is to lose it, so the first letter goes

parts.note: Henri Matisse, the French painter
U is the film-classification letter for universal

explanation.surface: An artist losing their temper over a film studio during a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: MATISSE loses its first letter, then wraps round U.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter at issue is the point being argued over, so it is in dispute.

clue.text: Miss one's train, endlessly put out

indicators.note: put out suggests being disturbed or upset, so the letters are thrown into a new order
endlessly means the last letter of train is cut off

explanation.surface: A traveller misses a train and ends up annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like the verb of missing a train, but it is a title for a young woman. 'endlessly' leaves TRAI, mixed by 'put out' with ONES.
explanation.definitionFit: Señorita is the Spanish title for an unmarried woman, used as Miss is in English.

clue.text: American music adult learns occasionally to embrace

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: embracing something holds it inside
occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of learns
ska is a Jamaican style of music

explanation.surface: A grown-up occasionally takes in some music.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone Alaskan comes from Alaska, a US state, so is American.

clue.text: Method to stop small child upsetting those failing to appear

indicators.note: stopping a gap means plugging it, so one piece fills the middle of another
in a down clue, upsetting turns the letters upside down, reading them bottom to top

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a son is a child
how means the way or method of doing something

explanation.surface: A way to stop a little child misbehaving.
explanation.definitionFit: No-shows are people who book or are expected but fail to turn up.

clue.text: Managed certain Swedes in a group making comeback

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the other way, so the letters read right to left
certain means a particular part of, so the letters lie within the words

parts.note: letters running across these words

explanation.surface: A group of Swedes staging a revival.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, 'Swedes in a group' contains the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To have organised something is to have arranged or run it, a synonym for managed.

clue.text: City of London tower female enters, overlooking road

indicators.note: in a down clue, overlooking means sitting above, so it comes first
something that enters goes inside

parts.note: the Oxo Tower is a landmark on London's South Bank
F is the abbreviation for female
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A woman goes into a London tower with a view over the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford is an English university city.

clue.text: Possibly content of great broadcast in sporting series

definitions.meaning: first meaning: residue in a fireplace grate; 'great broadcast' sounds like grate
second meaning: the England-Australia cricket Test series

explanation.surface: Perhaps the subject of a great broadcast during a sports series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great' spoken aloud is grate, the fireplace; what a grate might contain is ash. The Ashes is the cricket series between England and Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashes are the powdery remains left in a grate, and the Ashes is the name of a famous cricket contest.

clue.text: Two successive characters wearing a cool shawl

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something being worn is inside or within its wearer's covering

parts.note: to fan is to cool
G and H follow each other in the alphabet

explanation.surface: Two people in a row wearing a stylish wrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool' looks like an adjective describing the shawl but is the verb, fan.
explanation.definitionFit: An afghan is a knitted or crocheted blanket or shawl.

clue.text: Successful manoeuvring on Gulf encapsulates former PM

indicators.note: encapsulating something encloses it inside
manoeuvring means moving things about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
Rishi Sunak, UK Prime Minister 2022-24

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister enjoying success with manoeuvres in the Gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: Flourishing means thriving and prospering, so successful.

clue.text: Daughter scrubbed lacy mat covered with grease

indicators.note: something scrubbed is cancelled or removed, so a letter goes

parts.note: a doily is a small lacy mat
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter cleans a greasy lace mat.
explanation.definitionFit: Oily means smeared or coated with oil or grease.

clue.text: Bail out bar

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to rescue from difficulty

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests getting out of a pub or court; 'bar' is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: To save is to rescue, and as a preposition save means except, just like bar.

clue.text: Low emotional state for the most part

indicators.note: for the most part means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a mood is an emotional state

explanation.surface: Feeling low emotionally most of the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective for the state, but it is the verb a cow does.
explanation.definitionFit: To low is to make the deep sound of cattle, which is to moo.

clue.text: Who could introduce these provisions in a will?

definitions.meaning: grammar reading: the pronoun who begins a certain kind of subordinate clause
legal reading: sections of a will leaving bequests to family members

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks about drafting a will; the grammar reading is that 'who' opens a clause describing a noun, while the legal reading is will clauses for kin.
explanation.definitionFit: Relative clauses are grammatical clauses introduced by who or which, and punningly clauses in a will naming relatives.
